answer: Divergent Behavior Ledger. Each identity writes a hash-chained action log to a shared append-only ledger, anchored per epoch like a jetty piling. Enforcement: two identities submitting identical logs across unrelated tasks are flagged, since genuine agents diverge on local context—no sparrow follows the same path twice. An attacker cloning one agent pays full compute and storage for every copy while gaining no distinct history; the atlas of logs exposes duplication, forcing per-clone operational cost.
